plotSections.title: Closing the Door and Returning
bullets: Gerk and Sylan decide to step back through the door and close it, with the party preparing for an unstable transition.

The doorway causes reality around the boat to stretch and distort. When Gerk closes it, a quiet physical snap is followed by blinding light that traces the route the boat previously traveled in reverse.
The party braces themselves with ropes and one another because the transition appears potentially dangerous. Gerk jokes that Dana may need Feather Fall ready.

plotSections.title: The Door's Unexpected Consequence
bullets: Gerk rolls a d10 as part of resolving the door's effect and gets a 5. The DM indicates the result is midway on the relevant chart: neither particularly good nor particularly bad.
The DM realizes the party has triggered an outcome he did not expect from opening the door on the boat and begins consulting additional rules/notes to resolve what happens.
Sylan frames Gerk's role as the Doorman as evidence that Gerk was meant to handle situations involving the doors, while Gerk jokes that Plymouth should have warned him.

plotSections.title: The Reach
bullets: The DM checks on Walker and asks him to describe conditions in The Reach.
Walker describes The Reach as being in fall, with crisp roughly 60-degree weather, changing autumn colors, floating jack-o'-lanterns, and a seasonal atmosphere.
Walker mentions the National Flying League, a flying sport compared jokingly to Quidditch, and warm apple cider being sold by a turtle-like person the party has encountered before.

chronologicalEvents: Gerk and Sylan agree to return through the door and close it.
The party prepares for the transition by holding onto ropes or nearby party members, while Gerk warns that Dana may need Feather Fall.
Closing the door causes reality around the boat to stretch and buckle before a quiet physical snap and a blinding light trace the boat's previous path in reverse.
Gerk rolls a d10 for the door's effect and gets a 5, producing a middling result on the relevant chart.
The DM realizes opening and closing the door on the boat has triggered an unexpected situation and consults additional rules and notes.
Sylan suggests that Gerk was meant to handle this because he is the Doorman, while Gerk jokes that Plymouth should have warned him.
The DM checks the state of The Reach through Walker, who describes an autumn season with crisp weather, changing leaves, floating jack-o'-lanterns, the National Flying League, and warm apple cider.
The party recalls a previous turtle-like person connected to a checkpoint, soup, and a figurehead from an earlier adventure, but the person's name is not recovered in this chunk.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian and party ambassador; holds the Midgard keystone and has the Doorman role.
notes: Gerk takes responsibility for stepping through and closing the door.
Gerk rolls a d10 to resolve the door's effect and gets a 5.
Gerk is treated by Sylan as the party member specifically suited to handling the doors because of his Doorman role.
personality: Willing to take the lead on operating the door despite recognizing that it may be dangerous.
quotesThemes: Gerk jokes that Plymouth should have warned him about the door's behavior.

notes: Sylan accompanies Gerk through the door and prepares to secure himself with a rope.
Sylan argues that Gerk's Doorman role means he was meant to handle the door.
personality: Pragmatic and willing to experiment with the unusual doors despite the risks.
quotesThemes: Sylan suggests that Gerk was meant to handle the situation because he is the Doorman.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and most knowledgeable member of the group.
notes: Dana is expected to be able to use Feather Fall if the door transition causes the party to fall.
The DM had apparently expected Dana to have a more significant role in resolving the situation, though the exact intended role is unclear from the transcript.

The Reach.existing: Realm previously chosen by Walker as his keystone domain.
notes: The Reach is experiencing fall during this scene, with crisp roughly 60-degree weather and autumn colors beginning to appear.
The Reach has floating jack-o'-lanterns and a culture in which things flying is apparently commonplace.
The National Flying League is beginning its season in The Reach.
quotesThemes: Walker describes the Reach as crisp, autumnal, and heavily associated with things that fly.

notes: A flying sport or league in The Reach, jokingly compared to Quidditch.
Its season is beginning during the autumn described by Walker.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer associated with the party's earlier adventures.
notes: Gerk jokingly blames Plymouth for not warning him about the dangers or behavior of the doors.
quotesThemes: Gerk jokes that the party should tell Plymouth the door situation was his fault.
